shared_anchors: Gov. Ron DeSantis signed death warrant Friday
novel_facts: Marc Raczkoski (brother) identified and interviewed on camera
Brother's 40-year emotional journey and reaction to death warrant
Detail that execution would be Florida's 18th this year following 19 in 2025
Sheriff Flowers plans to attend execution and wants last thing Reaves sees to be deputy uniform
Concerns raised by Floridians Against the Death Penalty about execution pace
Family impact details: no more Christmas trees, holidays never the same

material_update_promotion_decisions.reason: Same event: both articles cover the death warrant signed by DeSantis for William Reaves for the 1986 killing of Deputy Raczkoski. Material update: the incoming article provides significant new information including an on-camera interview with the victim's brother Marc Raczkoski sharing his 40-year journey and reaction, Sheriff Flowers' plan to attend the execution with specific quote about wanting Reaves to see the uniform, context about Florida's execution pace (18th this year, 19 in 2025), and concerns from death penalty opposition groups. These are substantive additions that change what readers know about the community and official response to the death warrant. However, this remains a reaction/response story to the same underlying event (the death warrant signing) rather than an independently newsworthy follow-up, so it should update the canonical.

lead_independence.headline: Indian River County deputy and K9 Penny rescue missing dementia patient in Gadsden County
lead_independence.lead: Deputy Sam Lewis and his bloodhound K9 Penny helped rescue a missing 84-year-old woman with dementia during a multi-county search in Gadsden County near Tallahassee. Body camera footage captured Deputy Lewis scaling down trees into a ditch in a heavily wooded area before pulling the woman from shallow water approximately 30 hours after she disappeared.
